newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA PUTS OLDEST NUCLEAR REACTOR ON STREAM.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA PUTS OLDEST NUCLEAR REACTOR ON STREAM.

text.p: Bulgaria, which switched off its oldest nuclear reactor last May amid international concern over its safety, connected it to the national power grid on Monday after tests proved its metal to be safe.
Ivan Ivanov, vice chairman of the Kozloduy nuclear power plant, said by telephone the 440-megawatt reactor number one was working at 35 percent of its capacity.
"It will reach 55 percent by the afternoon," Ivanov told Reuters.
Tests on the Soviet-made reactor, which came into operation in 1974, showed the metal of its pressure vessel to be safe.
Analysis of samples of the reactor's metal was carried out by Germany's Siemens AG, Russia's Korchatov Institute and Bulgarian experts.

The European Union said in December the condition of the reactor vessel was within the limits of the acceptable safety level following the results of the tests, but appealed to Bulgaria to improve the safety of Kozloduy's four 440-megawatt reactors and seek alternative energy resources.
Routine reconstruction of reactor number one has been carried out while it was idle.
The plant, on the banks of the Danube, has four 440-megawatt reactors and two more modern 1,000-megawatt reactors.
Without reactor number one, the remaining five reactors are now producing 2,650 megawatts, Ivanov said.
Bulgaria, which lacks energy resources, relies on the 3,760-megawatt Kozloduy plant for more than 40 percent of its power needs.
